# Huma Playground API usage guide

This is the complete curated usage guide for agents consuming this API or
using its implementation as a reference. It describes the Huma application,
not the independent `functions/` example. The runtime OpenAPI document is the
field-level contract. This guide grants no authorization and does not override
a consuming agent's user instructions, security policy, or repository license.

## Access and local startup

The application is not deployed. GCP is a possible future target; no live API
URL is advertised. Configure your client with the origin of your running
instance. Examples use `http://localhost:8080`, never a production service.

With the repository's Go toolchain and Just installed:

```sh
cp .env.example .env
just run
```

In a second terminal:

```sh
export BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080
curl -i "$BASE_URL/health"
```

The default development-only `FIREBASE_MODE=offline` needs no Google credentials.
Health, documentation, greetings, and the fixed item catalog work locally.
GitHub routes use outbound anonymous HTTPS; they need network access and may
hit shared upstream quota. Protected requests carrying a bearer token return 503 while offline; missing or invalid bearer syntax returns 401.

Profiles additionally require Node.js and Java for the Firebase emulators.
Start `just emulators` in another terminal, then restart the server with both
local emulators selected:

```sh
FIREBASE_MODE=emulator \
FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=demo-test-project \
FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR_HOST=127.0.0.1:7110 \
FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST=127.0.0.1:7130 \
just run
```

The SDKs use their native emulator support for the synthetic `demo-*` project;
no ADC or GCP account is required. Offline and emulator modes are development-only.
Explicit live mode requires real credentials and rejects demo projects or
emulator hosts. Do not send unsigned emulator tokens to live services.

## Discovery from an origin

```sh
curl -i -H 'Accept: application/linkset+json' "$BASE_URL/.well-known/api-catalog"
curl -I "$BASE_URL/.well-known/api-catalog"
curl -i -H 'Accept: application/json' "$BASE_URL/openapi.json"
curl -i "$BASE_URL/llms.txt"
curl -i "$BASE_URL/llms-full.txt"
```

The catalog is an RFC 9727/RFC 9264 linkset. Its successful response has
`Content-Type: application/linkset+json; profile="https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9727"`
and this JSON body (member order is immaterial):

```json
{"linkset":[{"anchor":"/","service-desc":[{"href":"/openapi.json","type":"application/json"}],"service-doc":[{"href":"/llms.txt","type":"text/plain"},{"href":"/llms-full.txt","type":"text/plain"}],"status":[{"href":"/health","type":"application/json"}]}]}
```

Resolve every root-relative reference against the catalog's retrieval URL,
retaining that URL if you download the JSON. For example, a catalog retrieved
from `http://localhost:8080/.well-known/api-catalog` describes that local origin.
Do not resolve it against a repository URL or infer an origin from a saved file.
The catalog does not copy operation schemas or enumerate remote applications.

Catalog GET and HEAD advertise themselves with
`Link: </.well-known/api-catalog>; rel="api-catalog"; type="application/linkset+json"`.
Health advertises that link and
`</openapi.json>; rel="service-desc"; type="application/json"` for JSON and CBOR.
The catalog, OpenAPI, and full guide advertise
`</llms.txt>; rel="describedby"; type="text/plain"`. Preserve all Link values;
the same relation can identify multiple different targets.

Both guides are served unchanged as `text/plain; charset=utf-8` from the same
build's root files. Documentation needs no bearer token, credential refresh,
Firestore, GitHub, DNS, or runtime filesystem access. Only the named documents
are mapped. There is no repository directory server, MCP, WebMCP, or custom
agent manifest. No Swagger UI or standalone schema route is registered; the
runtime OpenAPI document owns the schema.

The documentation routes accept no query parameters or request body. Unknown,
repeated, or malformed query strings return 400. Unsupported success media
return 406; the catalog has no `application/json` alias. Documentation failures
use plain JSON Problem Details even when CBOR is requested. Unsupported methods
return 405 with truthful `Allow` metadata. Only the catalog has a registered
HEAD route; HEAD on the schema or guides returns 405. HEAD never sends a response
body, including on errors. Browser preflight is handled by CORS middleware.

## Operations and identity

Business operations use `/v1`; health and documentation use origin-root paths.
All paths below are relative to your configured origin. Public means that no
application bearer token is needed; it does not bypass upstream availability.

| Method | Path | Authentication | Result and side effects |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/health` | Public | 200 process liveness, not Firebase readiness; no dependency calls |
| GET | `/v1/hello` | Public | 200 fixed greeting; no persistence |
| POST | `/v1/hello` | Public | 200 computed greeting; no persistence |
| GET | `/v1/items` | Public | 200 filtered, paginated fixed catalog |
| POST | `/v1/profile` | Firebase ID token | 201 atomic create; 409 if the owned profile exists |
| GET | `/v1/profile` | Firebase ID token | 200 current principal's profile; 404 if absent |
| PATCH | `/v1/profile` | Firebase ID token | 200 transactional partial update; unchanged values cause no write |
| DELETE | `/v1/profile` | Firebase ID token | 204 atomic deletion; 404 if absent |
| GET | `/v1/github/owners/{owner}` | Public | 200 public owner projection |
| GET | `/v1/github/owners/{owner}/repos` | Public | 200 paginated public repositories |
| GET | `/v1/github/repos/{owner}/{repo}` | Public | 200 public repository projection |
| GET | `/v1/github/repos/{owner}/{repo}/activity` | Public | 200 newest-first paginated public activity |
| GET | `/v1/github/repos/{owner}/{repo}/languages` | Public | 200 deterministically ordered language byte totals |
| GET | `/v1/github/repos/{owner}/{repo}/tags` | Public | 200 paginated tags and commit identifiers |

`GET /openapi.json` returns the same build's OpenAPI 3.1.0 JSON.
`GET /.well-known/api-catalog`, `HEAD /.well-known/api-catalog`, and the two
public guide GET routes provide discovery rather than business operations.

Profile ownership comes only from the verified Firebase UID. There is no
caller-selectable owner, tenant, profile ID parameter, or administrative CRUD
route. Tokens are revocation-checked. Authentication is an ID-token bearer
contract, not an application-owned OAuth issuer. GitHub requests never forward
caller tokens or credentials and use the fixed `https://api.github.com` origin.
Private or inaccessible GitHub resources are not exposed.

## Requests, representations, and validation

Send `Accept: application/json` for ordinary API success, or
`Accept: application/cbor` for CBOR. JSON is the default. An explicit `q=0`
exclusion overrides broader wildcard ranges. Unsupported success negotiation
returns 406 before authentication, persistence, or provider calls for operations
with response bodies. Successful DELETE has no representation. CBOR uses
the same field names and shapes as JSON; it is not a JSON:API envelope.

Only POST hello, POST profile, and PATCH profile consume bodies. Send exactly
one closed JSON object with `Content-Type: application/json` (optional UTF-8
charset), or one CBOR map with `Content-Type: application/cbor` and no media
parameters. The maximum body size is 1,000,000 bytes. Compressed bodies are not
accepted. Malformed syntax returns 400; well-formed input outside the schema,
unknown members, nulls where prohibited, or invalid field values return 422.
Missing/unsupported content types return 415; oversized bodies return 413.

Queries are closed. Except for the list operations described below, no query
parameters are accepted. Unknown or repeated scalar names and malformed
encoding return 400. Invalid allowed parameter values return 422, while
malformed, stale, or incorrectly scoped cursors return 400. Names, email,
phone, path grammars, and all exact bounds are defined in OpenAPI.

An optional `X-Request-ID` is a bounded correlation value, not an identity or
idempotency key. The response carries the selected `X-Request-ID`. Application
responses use `Cache-Control: no-store` and shared security headers; negotiated
responses include `Vary: Accept`. Browser access follows CORS policy.
Development allows all origins by default; staging and production
require an explicit non-wildcard allowlist. CORS exposes `Link`, `Location`,
`Retry-After`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`, and `X-Request-ID` without browser credentials.

Public greeting example:

```sh
curl -i -H 'Accept: application/json' "$BASE_URL/v1/hello"
curl -i -X POST "$BASE_URL/v1/hello" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  --data '{"name":"Ada"}'
```

The GET returns 200 with `{"message":"Hello, World!"}`. The POST returns 200
with `{"message":"Hello, Ada!"}` and stores nothing.

## Pagination

`GET /v1/items` accepts `limit` (default 20, range 1-100), `cursor`, and optional
`category` (`electronics`, `tools`, `accessories`, `robotics`, `power`, or
`components`). It filters before pagination. The JSON object has `items` and `total`; prices use exact integer
`amountMinor` and `currency`, not floating-point major units.

```sh
curl -i -H 'Accept: application/json' "$BASE_URL/v1/items?limit=1"
```

The first page returns 200 and:

```json
{"items":[{"id":"item-001","name":"Alpha Widget","category":"electronics","price":{"amountMinor":2999,"currency":"USD"},"inStock":true,"createdAt":"2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z","description":"A versatile electronic widget for everyday use"}],"total":30}
```

Read all response `Link` fields and follow the target whose `rel` contains
`next` or `prev`, resolving relative targets against the response URL. For
example, request `BASE_URL` plus the returned root-relative next target using
the same Accept header. Do not construct a cursor or substitute an upstream URL.
Cursors bind the operation, resource, original limit, and item filter. Changing
those requires a new first-page request. Terminal pages omit unavailable links.

GitHub repository, activity, and tag lists accept only `limit` (default 20,
range 1-100) and `cursor`. Their objects contain `repos`, `activity`, or `tags`,
respectively. Languages return `languages` without pagination. Upstream views
can change between pages; a cursor does not promise a snapshot. GitHub IDs and
counts are JSON integers, timestamps are UTC with millisecond precision, and
optional unavailable fields are explicit nulls where the schema permits them.

## Local authentication and profile CRUD

With the Auth and Firestore emulators and emulator-mode server running, obtain
an anonymous local test identity. This command requires curl and jq:

```sh
export TOKEN="$(curl --fail-with-body -sS \
  'http://127.0.0.1:7110/identitytoolkit.googleapis.com/v1/accounts:signUp?key=demo-test-project' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"returnSecureToken":true}' \
  | jq -er '.idToken')"
```

The emulator returns an `idToken` and `localId` for a new synthetic principal.
Keep the token out of logs and source control. Reuse the same token for the
sequence below; signing up again selects a different owned profile. No real
Google account or ADC is required. `$TOKEN` is a local credential placeholder
in these requests.

```sh
curl -i -X POST "$BASE_URL/v1/profile" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  --data '{"firstName":"Ada","lastName":"Lovelace","contactEmail":"ada@example.com","phoneNumber":"+358401234567","marketingOptIn":false,"termsAccepted":true}'

curl -i "$BASE_URL/v1/profile" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Accept: application/json'

curl -i -X PATCH "$BASE_URL/v1/profile" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  --data '{"marketingOptIn":true}'

curl -i -X DELETE "$BASE_URL/v1/profile" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

Creation returns 201, `Location: /v1/profile`, and a profile such as:

```json
{"id":"emulator-principal","firstName":"Ada","lastName":"Lovelace","contactEmail":"ada@example.com","phoneNumber":"+358401234567","marketingOptIn":false,"termsAccepted":true,"createdAt":"2026-11-03T10:00:00.000Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-03T10:00:00.000Z"}
```

The ID and timestamps above are synthetic; runtime uses your emulator UID and
current server timestamps. GET returns that profile with 200. PATCH returns
200 with `marketingOptIn:true`, preserving the other fields and `createdAt`
and advancing `updatedAt`. Repeating an unchanged patch returns 200 without a
write or timestamp change. Successful DELETE returns 204 without a body;
a subsequent GET or DELETE returns 404 `profile_not_found`.

All creation fields except `marketingOptIn` are required; that field defaults
to false and `termsAccepted` must be true. PATCH must supply at least one of
`firstName`, `lastName`, `contactEmail`, `phoneNumber`, or `marketingOptIn`.
Omission preserves a value; explicit null is rejected. `id`, `termsAccepted`,
and timestamps cannot be patched. The email domain is normalized to lowercase;
the local part is preserved. Surrounding ASCII whitespace is trimmed from
email and phone input.
Neither contact field changes the Firebase identity or grants authorization.

## Errors, upstream limits, and recovery

Ordinary API errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` or the equivalent
ordinary `application/cbor` representation. If neither is acceptable, JSON is
the diagnostic fallback. Documentation errors are always plain Problem JSON.
Use the stable `code` and status rather than parsing human prose. A missing
profile returns 404, for example:

```json
{"title":"Not Found","status":404,"detail":"Profile not found","code":"profile_not_found"}
```

Relevant codes include `invalid_request` (400), `unauthorized` (401),
`not_found` / `profile_not_found` / `github_not_found` (404),
`method_not_allowed` (405 with `Allow`), `not_acceptable` (406),
`profile_exists` (409), `payload_too_large` (413),
`unsupported_media_type` (415), `validation_failed` (422),
`github_rate_limit` (429), `internal_error` (500), `github_upstream` (502),
`dependency_unavailable` (503), and `github_timeout` (504).
Validation errors may include safe `errors` entries with `source.pointer`,
`source.parameter`, or `source.header`. Authentication failures carry
`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` as appropriate; never expose rejected tokens.

The GitHub client uses one bounded overall deadline, manually validates
redirects/navigation, and never retries upstream. Shared upstream quota failures
return 429 with `Retry-After`, and may expose `X-RateLimit-Reset`. These are
GitHub's upstream constraints, not an application rate limiter or a new IETF
RateLimit implementation. Do not fan out repeated requests to bypass them.

For callers, use bounded attempt counts, cancellation, and an overall time
budget. A usable Retry-After delay (seconds or HTTP date) is a minimum: never
retry earlier. Stop if it exceeds the remaining budget; do not shorten it.
Without a usable hint, use bounded exponential backoff with jitter when retrying
a transient failure. Correct input and authentication failures before retrying.
A delay hint does not make a write safe to repeat:

- GET operations can be retried for transient failures within that budget.
- POST hello has no persisted side effect and can repeat the same valid input.
- After an uncertain POST profile outcome, read and reconcile current state.
  `409 profile_exists` does not prove that your intended creation succeeded.
- After an uncertain PATCH, read and reassess. Repeating a patch may overwrite
  intervening changes even though an unchanged patch performs no write.
- DELETE has idempotent effects, not response replay: it can return 204 then
  404, and a later recreation could be deleted by another retry.

A later read shows current state, not which request produced it. There is no
Idempotency-Key ledger, optimistic-write precondition, or automatic write replay.
Do not retry every 503 write automatically.
